BLOCKER: empty_delta_rule excludes engineering/** and data/backlog/** (config/id-blocks.json, baseline) purely by path class with no verification: a code/logic change committed into an excluded path yields "no review-relevant changes", exit 0, and is never reviewed (fail-open bypass).

Excluded-path classification is asserted by convention ("no hand-edited code in engineering/**") but nothing in the design detects or rejects hand-edits/stale content in those paths; generation must be drift-checked or content-class verified before the delta gate can trust the exclusion.
MAJOR: Delta base validity is under-specified: no ancestry/merge-base check that last_reviewed_head is an ancestor of HEAD; after rebase/squash/force-push the delta diff is misleading. DELTA_BASE_INVALID exists but does not define this case.

No re-baseline trigger: nothing forces a periodic full re-review (long delta chains, model/provider change, base divergence), so delta drift accumulates and unchanged-code interactions are only covered by AC-context text.
failure_matrix lacks a prior-evidence failure case: corrupt/missing/unparsable prior findings evidence should fail closed or force a full re-review, not silently degrade delta context.

Committed generated artifact engineering/design/<ID>.md has no drift/regeneration check, so stale or hand-edited design docs pass both Gate 1 and precheck and are also invisible to the delta diff (excluded path).

Reviewer prompt ingests repo/design/prior-findings content with no untrusted-content or prompt-injection handling and no provider endpoint pinning; evidence integrity depends wholly on provider behaviour.
Rollback direction of evidence_compat is one-way: old-tooling readability of new records is stated; behaviour of reverted tooling reading new-format evidence after a revert is not.
MINOR: Candidate ordering "collisions resolve by latest at" depends on wall-clock timestamps; prefer content/sequence-derived ordering even under the single-writer assumption.
Encoding gate scans the changed set only, so a BOM in previously committed files is never re-detected; document as accepted or add an opt-in full-tree scan.
"Full-candidate AC evidence" inside a delta-bounded prompt conflicts with the performance invariant; bound/paginate or store a reference rather than inlining.
No stated maximum size/streaming strategy for large diffs, encoding scans, or design-pack checks; large items may blow prompt or scan budgets.
Concurrency invariant relies on AGENTS IS-PF-0036 convention only; no lock or detection of a second writer on the same tree.
Reviewer egress is unpinned (base URL/model not fixed in config); a config drift silently changes the review channel.
NIT: Rollback mentions "generated design MDs deleted" without a removal command or file list; add to rollout steps.
Ownership/update cadence of config/design-pack.json (enforce_items/enforce_from) is not assigned.
Security section lists explicit N/A items without a verification hook; keep but add a re-check trigger if tooling gains network scope.
SUMMARY: Design is structurally strong: invariants, failure matrix, guardrail coverage, and language-rule compliance (tooling Python) are clear, and recurring findings (render/disposition tests) are pre-empted.
Top risk is review-integrity bypass via path-class exclusions without content verification, followed by delta-base validity under history rewrite and the absence of a re-baseline trigger.
Recommend tightening empty-delta trust, adding ancestry + prior-evidence failure cases and a generated-doc drift check before implementation.

rereview_reason: one-review budget + guardrails/learnings; final design review
